title.en: Hereditary House of Weizi of Song
title.raw: 《宋微子世家》 Hereditary House of Weizi of Song

sentences.zh: 微子開者，殷帝乙之首子而帝紂之庶兄也。

translations.literal: Wei Zi Kai was Emperor Yi of Yin's eldest son and Emperor Zhou's elder half-brother.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zi Kai was the first son of Emperor Yi of Yin and the elder half-brother of Emperor Zhou.

sentences.zh: 紂既立，不明，淫亂於政，微子數諫，紂不聽。

translations.literal: Zhou was already established but unenlightened. He was licentious and chaotic in government. Wei Zi frequently admonished him, but Zhou would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou was already on the throne, but he was unenlightened and chaotic in government. Wei Zi repeatedly admonished him, but Zhou would not listen.

sentences.zh: 及祖伊以周西伯昌之修德，滅黎國，懼禍至，以告紂。

translations.literal: When Zu Yi saw that Xi Bo Chang of Western Zhou was cultivating virtue and had destroyed the state of Li, he feared calamity was approaching and reported it to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Zu Yi saw that Xi Bo Chang, the Lord of the West of Zhou, was cultivating virtue and had destroyed the state of Li, he feared that calamity was approaching and reported it to Zhou.

sentences.zh: 紂曰：「我生不有命在天乎？

translations.literal: Zhou said: 'I born not have fate in heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Zhou said: "Do I not have my mandate from Heaven?

sentences.zh: 是何能為！」

translations.literal: This what can do!'
translations.idiomatic: What can they do to me!"

sentences.zh: 於是微子度紂終不可諫，欲死之，及去，未能自決，乃問於太師、少師曰：「殷不有治政，不治四方。

translations.literal: Then Wei Zi measured Zhou finally not admonishable, desired die for it, and go, not able self decide, then asked Tai Shi, Shao Shi said: 'Yin not have governing politics, not governing four directions.
translations.idiomatic: Then Weizi judged that Zhou could no longer be remonstrated with. He considered dying for the cause or leaving, but could not decide. He therefore asked the Grand Tutor and Junior Tutor, saying: "Yin has no orderly government and no longer governs the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 我祖遂陳於上，紂沈湎於酒，婦人是用，亂敗湯德於下。

translations.literal: Our ancestor displayed his achievements above. Zhou is immersed in wine and uses women, chaotically defeating Tang's virtue below.
translations.idiomatic: Our ancestor displayed his achievements on high, while Zhou is steeped in wine and given over to women, bringing Tang's virtue to ruin below.

sentences.zh: 殷既小大好草竊姦宄，卿士師師非度，皆有罪辜，乃無維獲，小民乃并興，相為敵讎。

translations.literal: Yin already, from small to great, delights in bandits, thieves, wicked evildoers. The qing and shi shi shi not according to measure, all have crime and guilt. Then there is no support to obtain. The small people then all rise up together, becoming enemies and foes to each other.
translations.idiomatic: From the smallest to the greatest, Yin delights in bandits, thieves, and wicked evildoers. The ministers and officers follow one another without measure, and all share guilt. There is no support left to rely on, and the common people rise up together, becoming enemies to one another.

sentences.zh: 今殷其典喪！

translations.literal: Now Yin its rules lost!
translations.idiomatic: Now Yin has lost its order!

sentences.zh: 若涉水无津涯。

translations.literal: Like fording water with no bank or shore.
translations.idiomatic: It is like fording water with no bank or shore.

sentences.zh: 殷遂喪，越至于今。」

translations.literal: Yin then perished, extend to now.'
translations.idiomatic: Yin is therefore losing itself, and the loss has reached the present day."

sentences.zh: 曰：「太師，少師，我其發出往？

translations.literal: Said: 'Tai Shi, Shao Shi, I should set out go?
translations.idiomatic: He said: "Grand Tutor, Junior Tutor, should I leave?

sentences.zh: 吾家保于喪？

translations.literal: My family preserve in perished?
translations.idiomatic: Can our house be preserved in a doomed state?

sentences.zh: 今女無故告予，顛躋，如之何其？」

translations.literal: Now you without reason tell me, fall stumble, like what how its?'
translations.idiomatic: Now you tell me this without cause, and I stumble in confusion. What should I do?"

sentences.zh: 太師若曰：「王子，天篤下菑亡殷國，乃毋畏畏，不用老長。

translations.literal: Tai Shi Ruo said: 'Prince, heaven thickly down calamity perish Yin state, then not fear fear, not use elders.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Tutor said: "Prince, Heaven has sent down heavy calamity to destroy the Yin state. The king does not fear what should be feared, and he does not employ his elders.

sentences.zh: 今殷民乃陋淫神祇之祀。

translations.literal: Now the Yin people are vulgar and licentious in sacrificing to the spirits and powers.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Yin people are vulgar and excessive in sacrificing to the spirits.

sentences.zh: 今誠得治國，國治身死不恨。

translations.literal: Now if I truly obtain to govern the state, govern the state and my body dies—I will not regret it.
translations.idiomatic: If I truly obtain the chance to govern the state, then even if I die after setting the state in order, I will have no regret.

sentences.zh: 為死，終不得治，不如去。」

translations.literal: For death, finally not obtain govern, not as good go.'
translations.idiomatic: If I die, I will never be able to govern. It is better to depart."

sentences.zh: 遂亡。

translations.literal: He then fled.
translations.idiomatic: He then fled.

sentences.zh: 箕子者，紂親戚也。

translations.literal: jizi was Zhou's kinsman.
translations.idiomatic: jizi was Zhou's kinsman.

sentences.zh: 紂始為象箸，箕子嘆曰：「彼為象箸，必為玉桮；

translations.literal: Zhou began make ivory chopsticks, jizi sighed said: 'He make ivory chopsticks, must make jade cup;
translations.idiomatic: Zhou began to make ivory chopsticks. Jizi sighed and said: "If he makes ivory chopsticks, he will surely make jade cups;

sentences.zh: 為桮，則必思遠方珍怪之物而御之矣。

translations.literal: To make a cup, one must then think of precious and strange things from distant places and use them.
translations.idiomatic: Once he makes such cups, he will surely think of precious and strange things from distant places and use them.

sentences.zh: 輿馬宮室之漸自此始，不可振也。」

translations.literal: Chariot horse palace chamber gradual from this begin, cannot revive.'
translations.idiomatic: The slide toward fine carriages and horses, palaces and mansions, begins here and cannot be checked."

sentences.zh: 紂為淫泆，箕子諫，不聽。

translations.literal: Zhou gave himself over to licentious excess. Jizi remonstrated, but he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou abandoned himself to debauchery. Jizi remonstrated with him, but he refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 人或曰：「可以去矣。」

translations.literal: Some said: 'You may leave.'
translations.idiomatic: Someone said: "You may leave."

sentences.zh: 箕子曰：「為人臣諫不聽而去，是彰君之惡而自說於民，吾不忍為也。」

translations.literal: jizi said: 'Be minister admonish not listen and go, is display lord evil and self please to people, I not endure do.'
translations.idiomatic: Jizi said: "When a minister remonstrates and is not heard, to leave is to expose the lord's evil and make oneself pleasing to the people. I cannot bear to do that."

sentences.zh: 乃被髪詳狂而為奴。

translations.literal: He then let his hair hang loose, feigned madness, and became a slave.
translations.idiomatic: He then let his hair hang loose, feigned madness, and lived as a slave.

sentences.zh: 遂隱而鼓琴以自悲，故傳之曰箕子操。

translations.literal: He then withdrew and played the zither to express his grief. It is therefore handed down as the jizi Cao.
translations.idiomatic: He then withdrew and played the zither to express his grief. The piece was therefore handed down as Jizi Cao.

sentences.zh: 王子比干者，亦紂之親戚也。

translations.literal: Prince Bi Gan was also Zhou's kinsman.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Bi Gan was also Zhou's kinsman.

sentences.zh: 見箕子諫不聽而為奴，則曰：「君有過而不以死爭，則百姓何辜！」

translations.literal: Saw jizi admonish not listen became slave, then said: 'Lord has error not with death contend, then hundred surnames what guilt!'
translations.idiomatic: He saw that Jizi had remonstrated without being heard and had reduced himself to slavery, and then said: "If a lord has faults and one does not contend with him even unto death, what wrong have the common people done?"

sentences.zh: 乃直言諫紂。

translations.literal: He then bluntly admonished Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then bluntly admonished Zhou.

sentences.zh: 紂怒曰：「吾聞聖人之心有七竅，信有諸乎？」

translations.literal: Zhou angered said: 'I heard sage person heart has seven apertures, truly has it?'
translations.idiomatic: Zhou was angry and said: "I have heard that a sage's heart has seven apertures. Is that truly so?"

sentences.zh: 乃遂殺王子比干，刳視其心。

translations.literal: He then killed Prince Bigan and cut him open to look at his heart.
translations.idiomatic: He then killed Prince Bigan and had his body cut open so he could inspect his heart.

sentences.zh: 微子曰：「父子有骨肉，而臣主以義屬。

translations.literal: Wei Zi said: 'Father son have bone flesh, minister lord with righteousness belong.
translations.idiomatic: Weizi said: "Father and son are bound by bone and flesh, while minister and lord are joined by righteousness.

sentences.zh: 故父有過，子三諫不聽，則隨而號之；

translations.literal: Therefore, father has error, son three admonish not listen, then follow cry for him;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, if a father errs and his son remonstrates three times without being heard, the son follows him and weeps for him;

sentences.zh: 人臣三諫不聽，則其義可以去矣。」

translations.literal: Minister three admonish not listen, then righteousness can go.'
translations.idiomatic: If a minister remonstrates three times and is not heard, then by righteousness he may leave."

sentences.zh: 於是太師、少師乃勸微子去，遂行。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Senior Tutor and Junior Tutor urged Wei Zi to leave, and he went.
translations.idiomatic: The Senior Tutor and Junior Tutor then urged Wei Zi to flee, and he did so.

sentences.zh: 周武王伐紂克殷，微子乃持其祭器造於軍門，肉袒面縛，左牽羊，右把茅，膝行而前以告。

translations.literal: King Wu of Zhou attacked Zhou and conquered Yin. Wei Zi then held his sacrificial vessels and went to the army gate, bared his flesh and bound his face, left hand leading a sheep, right hand grasping thatch, knee-walking forward to inform.
translations.idiomatic: King Wu of Zhou attacked Zhou and conquered Yin. Wei Zi then took his sacrificial vessels to the camp gate, bared his chest and bound his face, led a sheep with his left hand and held thatch in his right, and knelt forward to submit his petition.

sentences.zh: 於是武王乃釋微子，復其位如故。

translations.literal: Thereupon King Wu released Wei Zi and restored him to his former position.
translations.idiomatic: King Wu then released Wei Zi and restored him to his old rank.

sentences.zh: 武王封紂子武庚祿父以續殷祀，使管叔、蔡叔傅相之。

translations.literal: King Wu enfeoffed Zhou's son Wu Geng Lufu to continue the Yin sacrifices, and had Guan Shu and Cai Shu tutor and assist him.
translations.idiomatic: King Wu enfeoffed Zhou's son Wu Geng Lufu so the Yin sacrifices could continue, appointing Guan Shu and Cai Shu to guide and support him.

sentences.zh: 武王既克殷，訪問箕子。

translations.literal: King Wu had already conquered Yin and questioned jizi.
translations.idiomatic: After King Wu had conquered Yin, he consulted Jizi.

sentences.zh: 武王曰：「於乎！

translations.literal: Wu Wang said: 'Alas!
translations.idiomatic: King Wu said: "Alas!

sentences.zh: 維天陰定下民，相和其居，我不知其常倫所序。」

translations.literal: Only heaven secretly settles lower people, mutually harmonize their residence, I not know its constant order where arranged.'
translations.idiomatic: Heaven in hidden ways settles the people below and harmonizes their dwelling places. I do not know the constant order by which they are arranged."

sentences.zh: 箕子對曰：「在昔鯀陻鴻水，汨陳其五行，帝乃震怒，不從鴻範九等，常倫所斁。

translations.literal: jizi replied said: 'In former times Gun dammed great water, confused displayed its five phases, Emperor then angrily shook, not followed great pattern nine grades, constant order where abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Jizi replied: "In former times, Gun dammed the great flood and threw the five phases into confusion. The Emperor then grew wrathful; the Great Plan in its nine divisions was not followed, and the constant order was ruined.

sentences.zh: 鯀則殛死，禹乃嗣興。

translations.literal: Gun was put to death, and Yu then succeeded him and rose.
translations.idiomatic: Gun was executed, and Yu succeeded him and rose to prominence.

sentences.zh: 天乃錫禹鴻範九等，常倫所序。

translations.literal: Heaven then granted Yu the great pattern's nine grades, where the constant order was arranged.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven then granted Yu the Great Plan in its nine divisions, by which he arranged the constant order.

sentences.zh: 「初一曰五行；

translations.literal: 'First one called five phases;
translations.idiomatic: "The first is the five phases;

sentences.zh: 二曰五事；

translations.literal: Second called five matters;
translations.idiomatic: the second is called the five matters;

sentences.zh: 三曰八政；

translations.literal: Third called eight governments;
translations.idiomatic: the third is called the eight governments;

sentences.zh: 四曰五紀；

translations.literal: Fourth called five records;
translations.idiomatic: the fourth is called the five records;

sentences.zh: 五曰皇極；

translations.literal: Fifth called royal pole;
translations.idiomatic: the fifth is called the royal pole;

sentences.zh: 六曰三德；

translations.literal: Sixth called three virtues;
translations.idiomatic: the sixth is called the three virtues;

sentences.zh: 七曰稽疑；

translations.literal: Seventh called examine doubts;
translations.idiomatic: the seventh is called examining doubts;

sentences.zh: 八曰庶徵；

translations.literal: Eighth called many signs;
translations.idiomatic: the eighth is called the many signs;

sentences.zh: 九曰嚮用五福，畏用六極。

translations.literal: The ninth is called facing using the five blessings, fearing using the six extremes.
translations.idiomatic: the ninth concerns turning toward and using the five blessings, and standing in awe of and using the six extremes.

sentences.zh: 「五行：一曰水，二曰火，三曰木，四曰金，五曰土。

translations.literal: 'Five phases: one called water, two called fire, three called wood, four called metal, five called earth.
translations.idiomatic: The five phases: "first is water, second fire, third wood, fourth metal, fifth earth.

sentences.zh: 水曰潤下，火曰炎上，木曰曲直，金曰從革，土曰稼穡。

translations.literal: Water is called moistening downward. Fire is called flaming upward. Wood is called bending and straightening. Metal is called following change. Earth is called plowing and harvesting.
translations.idiomatic: Water moistens downward. Fire flames upward. Wood bends and straightens. Metal yields and changes. Earth is for sowing and reaping.

sentences.zh: 潤下作鹹，炎上作苦，曲直作酸，從革作辛，稼穡作甘。

translations.literal: Moistening downward makes salty. Flaming upward makes bitter. Bending and straightening makes sour. Following change makes pungent. Plowing and harvesting makes sweet.
translations.idiomatic: Moistening downward produces saltiness. Flaming upward produces bitterness. Bending and straightening produce sourness. Yielding and changing produce pungency. Sowing and reaping produce sweetness.

sentences.zh: 「五事：一曰貌，二曰言，三曰視，四曰聽，五曰思。

translations.literal: 'Five matters: one called appearance, two called speech, three called seeing, four called hearing, five called thinking.
translations.idiomatic: The five matters: "first is appearance, second speech, third sight, fourth hearing, fifth thought.

sentences.zh: 貌曰恭，言曰從，視曰明，聽曰聰，思曰睿。

translations.literal: Appearance is called respectful. Speech is called compliant. Seeing is called clear. Hearing is called acute. Thinking is called profound.
translations.idiomatic: Appearance is respectfulness. Speech is compliance. Sight is clarity. Hearing is acuity. Thought is profundity.

sentences.zh: 恭作肅，從作治，明作智，聰作謀，睿作聖。

translations.literal: Respectful makes solemn. Compliant makes orderly. Clear makes wise. Acute makes plans. Profound makes sage.
translations.idiomatic: Respectfulness produces solemnity. Compliance produces order. Clarity produces wisdom. Acuity produces planning. Profundity produces sageliness.

sentences.zh: 「八政：一曰食，二曰貨，三曰祀，四曰司空，五曰司徒，六曰司寇，七曰賓，八曰師。

translations.literal: 'Eight governments: one called food, two called goods, three called sacrifices, four called Sikong, five called Situ, six called Si Kou, seven called guests, eight called army.
translations.idiomatic: The eight affairs of government: "first food, second goods, third sacrifices, fourth the Minister of Works, fifth the Minister of Education, sixth the Minister of Justice, seventh guests, eighth the army.

sentences.zh: 「五紀：一曰歲，二曰月，三曰日，四曰星辰，五曰歷數。

translations.literal: 'Five records: one called year, two called month, three called day, four called stars planets, five called calendar numbers.
translations.idiomatic: The five records: "first the year, second the month, third the day, fourth the stars and planets, fifth calendar calculations.

sentences.zh: 「皇極：皇建其有極，斂時五福，用傅錫其庶民，維時其庶民于女極，錫女保極。

translations.literal: 'Royal pole: king establishes his having pole, gathers timely five blessings, uses spread grant his common people, only then his common people at your pole, grant you preserve pole.
translations.idiomatic: The royal standard: "the king establishes his standard, gathers the five blessings in due season, and uses them to spread gifts among the common people. The common people then follow your standard, and you are granted preservation of the standard.

sentences.zh: 凡厥庶民，毋有淫朋，人毋有比德，維皇作極。

translations.literal: All their common people shall not have licentious companions. People shall not have comparable virtue. Only the king makes the pole.
translations.idiomatic: Among all the common people, let there be no licentious factions and no one setting virtue beside the standard. Only the sovereign establishes the standard.

sentences.zh: 凡厥庶民，有猷有為有守，女則念之。

translations.literal: All their common people who have plans, have actions, have holdings—you then think of them.
translations.idiomatic: Among all the common people, when some have plans, actions, and constancy, you should keep them in mind.

sentences.zh: 不協于極，不離于咎，皇則受之。

translations.literal: Not agreeing at the pole, not separating at calamity—the king then accepts it.
translations.idiomatic: If they do not conform to the standard yet have not fallen into guilt, the sovereign accepts them.

sentences.zh: 而安而色，曰予所好德，女則錫之福。

translations.literal: Their peaceful appearance—said 'I what good virtue'—you then grant them blessings.
translations.idiomatic: Those who are peaceful in demeanor and say, "I love virtue," you then grant blessings.

sentences.zh: 時人斯其維皇之極。

translations.literal: Timely people—this is their only wang pole.
translations.idiomatic: Such people are what uphold the sovereign's standard.

sentences.zh: 毋侮寡而畏高明。

translations.literal: Do not insult the few and fear the high and bright.
translations.idiomatic: Do not insult the few or stand in fear of the high and brilliant.

sentences.zh: 人之有能有為，使羞其行，而國其昌。

translations.literal: People who have ability and action—make them advance their conduct, and the state will prosper.
translations.idiomatic: When people have ability and action, let them advance in their conduct, and the state will prosper.

sentences.zh: 凡厥正人，既富方穀。

translations.literal: All their upright people are already rich in each valley.
translations.idiomatic: All upright people, once enriched, will be good.

sentences.zh: 女不能使有好于而家，時人斯其辜。

translations.literal: You cannot make there be good in your family. Timely people—this is their crime.
translations.idiomatic: If you cannot make them love you and your house, then these people bear the fault.

sentences.zh: 于其毋好，女雖錫之福，其作女用咎。

translations.literal: At their not being good, though you grant them blessings, they will make you use calamity.
translations.idiomatic: If they do not love virtue, then even if you grant them blessings, they will use them to bring calamity upon you.

sentences.zh: 毋偏毋頗，遵王之義。

translations.literal: Not partial, not inclined—follow the wang's righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Do not be partial, do not be biased; follow the king's righteousness.

sentences.zh: 毋有作好，遵王之道。

translations.literal: Do not have making good—follow the wang's way.
translations.idiomatic: Do not indulge private likes; follow the king's way.

sentences.zh: 毋有作惡，遵王之路。

translations.literal: Do not have making evil—follow the wang's road.
translations.idiomatic: Do not indulge private hates; follow the king's road.

sentences.zh: 毋偏毋黨，王道蕩蕩。

translations.literal: Not partial, not factional—the wang's way is broad and broad.
translations.idiomatic: Without partiality and without faction, the kingly way is broad.

sentences.zh: 毋黨毋偏，王道平平。

translations.literal: Not factional, not partial—the wang's way is level and level.
translations.idiomatic: Without faction and without partiality, the kingly way is level.

sentences.zh: 毋反毋側，王道正直。

translations.literal: Not contrary, not slanted—the wang's way is straight and upright.
translations.idiomatic: Without opposition and without leaning aside, the kingly way is straight and upright.

sentences.zh: 會其有極，歸其有極。

translations.literal: Gather their having a pole. Return their having a pole.
translations.idiomatic: Gather them to the standard; return them to the standard.

sentences.zh: 曰王極之傅言，是夷是訓，于帝其順。

translations.literal: The wang pole's spread words—this is even, this is instruction. To the emperor it is compliant.
translations.idiomatic: The words spread from the king's standard are balanced and instructive; they accord with the Thearch above.

sentences.zh: 凡厥庶民，極之傅言，是順是行，以近天子之光。

translations.literal: All their common people—the pole's spread words—this is compliant, this is action, to approach the Tian Zi's light.
translations.idiomatic: All the common people follow and practice the words spread from the standard, drawing near to the radiance of the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 曰天子作民父母，以為天下王。

translations.literal: It is said the Tian Zi makes himself the people's parents, to be the wang of the world.
translations.idiomatic: The text says that the Son of Heaven acts as father and mother to the people and thereby becomes king of the world.

sentences.zh: 「三德：一曰正直，二曰剛克，三曰柔克。

translations.literal: 'Three virtues: one called upright straight, two called firm overcome, three called gentle overcome.
translations.idiomatic: The three virtues: "first uprightness, second firm mastery, third gentle mastery.

sentences.zh: 平康正直，彊不友剛克，內友柔克，沈漸剛克，高明柔克。

translations.literal: Peace and calm are upright and straight. Strong but not friendly uses firm overcoming. Inner friendly uses gentle overcoming. Deep and gradual uses firm overcoming. High and bright uses gentle overcoming.
translations.idiomatic: In peace and calm, use uprightness. With the strong and unfriendly, use firm mastery. With the inwardly friendly, use gentle mastery. With the deeply sunk, use firm mastery. With the high and brilliant, use gentle mastery.

sentences.zh: 維辟作福，維辟作威，維辟玉食。

translations.literal: Only the ruler makes blessings. Only the ruler makes awe. Only the ruler has jade food.
translations.idiomatic: Only the ruler dispenses blessings. Only the ruler wields awe. Only the ruler eats jade-like food.

sentences.zh: 臣无有作福作威玉食。

translations.literal: Ministers shall not have making blessings, making awe, jade food.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers must not dispense blessings, wield awe, or enjoy jade-like food.

sentences.zh: 臣有作福作威玉食，其害于而家，凶于而國，人用側頗辟，民用僭忒。

translations.literal: If ministers have making blessings, making awe, jade food—it harms your family, is calamitous for your state. People use slanted and inclined rulers. People use presumptuous and deviant ways.
translations.idiomatic: If ministers dispense blessings, wield awe, or enjoy jade-like food, it harms your house and brings calamity to your state. The people will follow crooked and partial rulers, and the people will become presumptuous and deviant.

sentences.zh: 「稽疑：擇建立卜筮人。

translations.literal: 'Examine doubts: select establish divination people.
translations.idiomatic: Examining doubts: "select and appoint diviners.

sentences.zh: 乃命卜筮，曰雨，曰濟，曰涕，曰霧，曰克，曰貞，曰悔，凡七。

translations.literal: Then command divination: called rain, called aid, called tear, called fog, called overcome, called upright, called regret—altogether seven.
translations.idiomatic: Then command the divination: the signs are called rain, clearing, tears, mist, overcoming, correctness, and regret—seven in all.

sentences.zh: 卜五，占之用二，衍貣。

translations.literal: Divine five times, use two for the divination, extend greedily.
translations.idiomatic: There are five turtle-shell indications, and two milfoil indications are used with them, extending the set.

sentences.zh: 立時人為卜筮，三人占則從二人之言。

translations.literal: Establish timely people as divination, three people divine then follow two people's words.
translations.idiomatic: Appoint these people for turtle-shell and milfoil divination. If three people divine, follow the words of two.

sentences.zh: 女則有大疑，謀及女心，謀及卿士，謀及庶人，謀及卜筮。

translations.literal: You then have great doubt—plan reaching your heart, plan reaching the qing shi, plan reaching the common people, plan reaching divination.
translations.idiomatic: When you have great doubts, consult your own heart, consult the qing shi, consult the common people, and consult turtle-shell and milfoil divination.

sentences.zh: 女則從，龜從，筮從，卿士從，庶民從，是之謂大同，而身其康彊，而子孫其逢吉。

translations.literal: You then follow, turtle follows, divination follows, qing shi follow, common people follow—this is called great unity, and your body will be peaceful and strong, and your descendants will meet with auspiciousness.
translations.idiomatic: If you agree, the turtle agrees, the milfoil agrees, the qing shi agree, and the common people agree, this is called great concord; your person will be peaceful and strong, and your descendants will meet with good fortune.

sentences.zh: 女則從，龜從，筮從，卿士逆，庶民逆，吉。

translations.literal: You then follow, turtle follows, divination follows, qing shi are contrary, common people are contrary—auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: If you agree, the turtle agrees, and the milfoil agrees, while the qing shi and the common people are opposed, it is auspicious.

sentences.zh: 卿士從，龜從，筮從，女則逆，庶民逆，吉。

translations.literal: Qing shi follow, turtle follows, divination follows, you are contrary, common people are contrary—auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: If the qing shi agree, the turtle agrees, and the milfoil agrees, while you and the common people are opposed, it is auspicious.

sentences.zh: 庶民從，龜從，筮從，女則逆，卿士逆，吉。

translations.literal: Common people follow, turtle follows, divination follows, you are contrary, qing shi are contrary—auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: If the common people agree, the turtle agrees, and the milfoil agrees, while you and the qing shi are opposed, it is auspicious.

sentences.zh: 女則從，龜從，筮逆，卿士逆，庶民逆，作內吉，作外凶。

translations.literal: You then follow, turtle follows, divination is contrary, qing shi are contrary, common people are contrary—making inner affairs auspicious, making outer affairs inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: If you agree and the turtle agrees, while the milfoil, the qing shi, and the common people are opposed, inner affairs are auspicious and outer affairs are inauspicious.

sentences.zh: 龜筮共違于人，用靜吉，用作凶。

translations.literal: Turtle and divination together contrary to people—using quiet is auspicious, using action is inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: If both turtle shell and milfoil go against human judgment, remaining still is auspicious and taking action is inauspicious.

sentences.zh: 「庶徵：曰雨，曰陽，曰奧，曰寒，曰風，曰時。

translations.literal: 'Many signs: called rain, called sunshine, called warm, called cold, called wind, called season.
translations.idiomatic: "The many signs are rain, sunshine, warmth, cold, wind, and seasonableness.

sentences.zh: 五者來備，各以其序，庶草繁廡。

translations.literal: When the five arrive complete, each in its proper order, the many grasses grow thick and luxuriant.
translations.idiomatic: When all five arrive in their proper sequence, the grasses flourish in abundance.

sentences.zh: 一極備，凶。

translations.literal: One extreme prepared—inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: One extreme prepared—inauspicious.

sentences.zh: 一極亡，凶。

translations.literal: One extreme gone—inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: One extreme gone—inauspicious.

sentences.zh: 曰休徵：曰肅，時雨若，曰治，時暘若；

translations.literal: Called auspicious signs: called solemn, timely rain like, called orderly, timely sunshine like;
translations.idiomatic: The auspicious signs are these: solemnity, and timely rain follows; order, and timely sunshine follows;

sentences.zh: 曰知，時奧若；

translations.literal: Called wisdom, timely warm like;
translations.idiomatic: wisdom, and timely warmth follows;

sentences.zh: 曰謀，時寒若；

translations.literal: Called planning, timely cold like;
translations.idiomatic: planning, and timely cold follows;

sentences.zh: 曰聖，時風若。

translations.literal: Called sage, timely wind as it should be.
translations.idiomatic: sageliness, and timely wind follows.

sentences.zh: 曰咎徵：曰狂，常雨若；

translations.literal: Called calamitous signs: called madness, constant rain like;
translations.idiomatic: The calamitous signs are these: madness, and constant rain follows;

sentences.zh: 曰僭，常暘若；

translations.literal: Called usurpation, constant sunshine like;
translations.idiomatic: usurpation, and constant sunshine follows;

sentences.zh: 曰舒，常奧若；

translations.literal: Called laxity, constant warm like;
translations.idiomatic: laxity, and constant warmth follows;

sentences.zh: 曰急，常寒若；

translations.literal: Called urgency, constant cold like;
translations.idiomatic: urgency, and constant cold follows;

sentences.zh: 曰霧，常風若。

translations.literal: Called fog, constant wind as it should be.
translations.idiomatic: confusion, and constant wind follows.

sentences.zh: 王眚維歲，卿士維月，師尹維日。

translations.literal: The wang's blemish affects only the year. The qing shi affects only the month. The shi yin affects only the day.
translations.idiomatic: The king's errors affect the year; ministers' errors affect the month; officials' errors affect the day.

sentences.zh: 歲月日時毋易，百穀用成，治用明，畯民用章，家用平康。

translations.literal: Year, month, day, season do not change. The hundred grains mature. Governance is clear. Good people are manifest. Families are peaceful and healthy.
translations.idiomatic: Year, month, day, and season do not change. The hundred grains mature. Governance is clear. Good people are manifest. Families are peaceful and healthy.

sentences.zh: 日月歲時既易，百穀用不成，治用昏不明，畯民用微，家用不寧。

translations.literal: Day, month, year, season have already changed. The hundred grains do not mature. Governance is dark and not clear. Good people are subtle. Families are not peaceful.
translations.idiomatic: Day, month, year, and season have already changed. The hundred grains do not mature. Governance is dark and not clear. Good people are subtle. Families are not peaceful.

sentences.zh: 庶民維星，星有好風，星有好雨。

translations.literal: The common people are the stars: the stars favor wind, and the stars favor rain.
translations.idiomatic: The common people correspond to the stars: some stars favor wind, and some favor rain.

sentences.zh: 日月之行，有冬有夏。

translations.literal: The movement of sun and moon has winter and has summer.
translations.idiomatic: The movement of the sun and moon has winter and has summer.

sentences.zh: 月之從星，則以風雨。

translations.literal: When the moon follows the stars, it thereby brings wind and rain.
translations.idiomatic: When the moon follows the stars, wind and rain result.

sentences.zh: 「五福：一曰壽，二曰富，三曰康寧，四曰攸好德，五曰考終命。

translations.literal: 'Five blessings: one called longevity, two called wealth, three called peaceful healthy, four called practice good virtue, five called examine end life.
translations.idiomatic: The five blessings: "first longevity, second wealth, third health and peace, fourth love of virtue, fifth completing one's allotted lifespan.

sentences.zh: 六極：一曰凶短折，二曰疾，三曰憂，四曰貧，五曰惡，六曰弱。」

translations.literal: Six extremes: one called inauspicious short broken, two called illness, three called worry, four called poverty, five called evil, six called weak.'
translations.idiomatic: The six extremes: first misfortune and shortened life, second illness, third worry, fourth poverty, fifth evil, sixth weakness."

sentences.zh: 於是武王乃封箕子於朝鮮而不臣也。

translations.literal: Thereupon King Wu enfeoffed Jizi in Joseon but did not make him a subject.
translations.idiomatic: King Wu then enfeoffed Jizi in Joseon, while not treating him as a vassal.

sentences.zh: 其後箕子朝周，過故殷虛，感宮室毀壞，生禾黍，箕子傷之，欲哭則不可，欲泣為其近婦人，乃作麥秀之詩以歌詠之。

translations.literal: After that, jizi paid court to Zhou. Passing the former Yin ruins, he was moved by the ruined palaces and halls where millet and wheat now grew. jizi grieved. He wished to wail but could not; he wished to weep, but that seemed unseemly so near the women's quarters. He therefore composed the 'Wheat Ears' poem and sang it.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Jizi paid court to Zhou. Passing the former Yin ruins, he was moved by the ruined palaces and halls where millet and grain now grew. Jizi grieved. He wished to wail but could not; he wished to weep, but that seemed too close to women's mourning. He therefore composed the "Wheat Ears" poem and sang it.

sentences.zh: 其詩曰：「麥秀漸漸兮，禾黍油油。

translations.literal: The poem says: 'The wheat ears grow lush; the millet stands thick.
translations.idiomatic: The poem says: "The wheat ears grow lush; the millet stands thick.

sentences.zh: 彼狡僮兮，不與我好兮！」

translations.literal: That crafty lad—he would not befriend me!'
translations.idiomatic: That crafty lad—he would not befriend me!"

sentences.zh: 所謂狡童者，紂也。

translations.literal: What was called the crafty boy was Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: The so-called crafty boy was Zhou.

sentences.zh: 殷民聞之，皆為流涕。

translations.literal: When the Yin people heard it, they all shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: When the people of Yin heard the song, they all wept.

sentences.zh: 武王崩，成王少，周公旦代行政當國。

translations.literal: King Wu died; King Cheng was young, so the Duke of Zhou Dan acted in his place and administered the government, holding charge of the state.
translations.idiomatic: After King Wu died, King Cheng was still young, so the Duke of Zhou Dan governed in his stead and held the state together.

sentences.zh: 管、蔡疑之，乃與武庚作亂，欲襲成王、周公。

translations.literal: Guan and Cai doubted it. They then made rebellion with Wu Geng, desiring to attack King Cheng and the Duke of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guan and Cai doubted it. They then rebelled with Wu Geng, desiring to attack King Cheng and the Duke of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 周公既承成王命誅武庚，殺管叔，放蔡叔，乃命微子開代殷後，奉其先祀，作微子之命以申之，國于宋。

translations.literal: The Duke of Zhou had already received King Cheng's command to execute Wu Geng, kill Guan Shu, and banish Cai Shu. He then commanded Wei Zi Kai to replace the Yin descendants, offer their ancestor sacrifices, made the Wei Zi command to repeat it, and established the state at Song.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou had received King Cheng's command to execute Wu Geng, kill Guan Shu, and banish Cai Shu. He then ordered Weizi Kai to replace the Yin line, offer sacrifices to its ancestors, and established him in Song, issuing the Charge to Weizi to confirm it.

sentences.zh: 微子故能仁賢，乃代武庚，故殷之餘民甚戴愛之。

translations.literal: Wei Zi was therefore able to be benevolent and worthy. He then replaced Wu Geng. Therefore, Yin's remnant people greatly revered and loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Because Weizi was benevolent and worthy, he replaced Wu Geng, and the remnant people of Yin greatly revered and loved him.

sentences.zh: 釐公十七年，周厲王出奔彘。

translations.literal: In Duke Xi's seventeenth year, King Li of Zhou fled to Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Duke Xi, King Li of Zhou fled to Zhi.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，釐公卒，子惠公覵立。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, Duke Xi died, and his son Duke Hui Bi ascended.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year, Duke Xi died, and his son Duke Hui Bi succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 惠公四年，周宣王即位。

translations.literal: In Duke Hui's fourth year, King Xuan of Zhou took the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Duke Hui, King Xuan of Zhou ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 三十年，惠公卒，子哀公立。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, Duke Hui died, and his son Duke Ai ascended.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year, Duke Hui died, and his son Duke Ai succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 哀公元年卒，子戴公立。

translations.literal: Duke Ai died in his first year, and his son Duke Dai ascended.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Ai died in his first year, and his son Duke Dai succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 戴公二十九年，周幽王為犬戎所殺，秦始列為諸侯。

translations.literal: In Duke Dai's twenty-ninth year, King You of Zhou was killed by the Quan Rong. Qin began to be ranked as feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: In Duke Dai's twenty-ninth year, King You of Zhou was killed by the Quanrong. Qin was first ranked among the feudal lords.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，戴公卒，子武公司空立。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year, Duke Dai died, and his son Duke Wu Sikong ascended.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year, Duke Dai died, and his son Duke Wu Sikong succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 武公生女為魯惠公夫人，生魯桓公。

translations.literal: Duke Wu gave birth to a daughter who became Duke Hui of Lu's wife. She gave birth to Duke Huan of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Wu had a daughter who became the wife of Duke Hui of Lu and gave birth to Duke Huan of Lu.

sentences.zh: 十八年，武公卒，子宣公力立。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, Duke Wu died, and his son Duke Xuan Li ascended.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, Duke Wu died, and his son Duke Xuan Li succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 宣公有太子與夷。

translations.literal: Duke Xuan had a crown prince named Yuyi.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Xuan had a crown prince, Yuyi.

sentences.zh: 十九年，宣公病，讓其弟和，曰：「父死子繼，兄死弟及，天下通義也。

translations.literal: Nineteenth year, Xuan Gong ill, yielded his younger brother He, said: 'Father dies son succeeds, elder brother dies younger brother reaches, world common righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year, Duke Xuan fell ill. He yielded the succession to his younger brother He, saying: "When a father dies, the son succeeds; when an elder brother dies, the younger brother follows. This is the common principle of the world.

sentences.zh: 我其立和。」

translations.literal: I should establish He.'
translations.idiomatic: I should establish He."

sentences.zh: 和亦三讓而受之。

translations.literal: He also declined three times and then accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: He, too, declined three times before accepting.

sentences.zh: 宣公卒，弟和立，是為穆公。

translations.literal: Duke Xuan died, and his younger brother He was established; this was Duke Mu.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke Xuan died, his younger brother He succeeded him as Duke Mu.

sentences.zh: 穆公九年，病，召大司馬孔父謂曰：「先君宣公捨太子與夷而立我，我不敢忘。

translations.literal: Mu Gong ninth year, ill, summoned grand si ma Kong Fu told said: 'Former lord Xuan Gong abandoned crown prince Yu Yi established me, I dare not forget.
translations.idiomatic: In Duke Mu's ninth year, he fell ill. He summoned Grand Marshal Kong Fu and told him: "The former lord Duke Xuan set aside Crown Prince Yuyi and established me. I dare not forget this.

sentences.zh: 我死，必立與夷也。」

translations.literal: I die, must establish Yu Yi.'
translations.idiomatic: When I die, you must establish Yuyi."

sentences.zh: 孔父曰：「群臣皆願立公子馮。」

translations.literal: Kong Fu said: 'Multitude ministers all wish establish prince Ping.'
translations.idiomatic: Kong Fu said: "The ministers all wish to establish Prince Ping."

sentences.zh: 穆公曰：「毋立馮，吾不可以負宣公。」

translations.literal: Mu Gong said: 'Do not establish Ping, I cannot betray Xuan Gong.'
translations.idiomatic: Duke Mu said: "Do not establish Feng. I cannot betray Duke Xuan."

sentences.zh: 於是穆公使馮出居于鄭。

translations.literal: Thereupon Duke Mu sent Feng out to live in Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Mu then sent Feng away to reside in Zheng.

sentences.zh: 八月庚辰，穆公卒，兄宣公子與夷立，是為殤公。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, gengchen, Duke Mu died. His elder brother Duke Xuan's son Yu Yi ascended, who became Duke Shang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on gengchen, Duke Mu died. His elder brother Duke Xuan's son Yuyi ascended; this was Duke Shang.

sentences.zh: 君子聞之，曰：「宋宣公可謂知人矣，立其弟以成義，然卒其子復享之。

translations.literal: Gentleman heard it, said: 'Song Xuan Gong can be called knows people, established his younger brother to complete righteousness, yet finally his son again enjoyed it.
translations.idiomatic: A gentleman heard of it and said: "Duke Xuan of Song may be called one who understood men. He established his younger brother to fulfill righteousness, yet in the end his own son again enjoyed the state.

sentences.zh: 莊公元年，華督為相。

translations.literal: In Duke Zhuang's first year, Hua Du served as chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Duke Zhuang, Hua Du became chancellor.

sentences.zh: 九年，執鄭之祭仲，要以立突為鄭君。

translations.literal: Ninth year, seized Zheng's Ji Zhong, coerced to establish Tu as Zheng lord.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, they seized Zheng's Ji Zhong and coerced him to establish Tu as Zheng's lord.

sentences.zh: 祭仲許，竟立突。

translations.literal: Ji Zhong agreed, and in the end they established Tu.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Zhong agreed, and Tu was ultimately installed.

sentences.zh: 十九年，莊公卒，子湣公捷立。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, Duke Zhuang died, and his son Duke Min Jie ascended.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year, Duke Zhuang died, and his son Duke Min Jie succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 十年夏，宋伐魯，戰於乘丘，魯生虜宋南宮萬。

translations.literal: In the tenth year summer, Song attacked Lu and battled at Cheng Qiu. Lu captured Song's Nangong Wan alive.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, in summer, Song attacked Lu and fought at Chengqiu. Lu captured Song's Nangong Wan alive.

sentences.zh: 宋人請萬，萬歸宋。

translations.literal: The people of Song requested Wan, and Wan returned to Song.
translations.idiomatic: The Song people asked for Wan's return, and Wan came back to Song.

sentences.zh: 十一年秋，湣公與南宮萬獵，因博爭行，湣公怒，辱之，曰：「始吾敬若；

translations.literal: Eleventh year autumn, Min Gong with Nangong Wan hunted, because gambling contended route, Min Gong angered, humiliated him, said: 'Beginning I respected you;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, in autumn, Duke Min hunted with Nangong Wan. During a game they argued over the route. Duke Min became angry and humiliated him, saying: "At first I respected you;

sentences.zh: 今若，魯虜也。」

translations.literal: Now you, Lu captive.'
translations.idiomatic: now you are a captive of Lu."

sentences.zh: 萬有力，病此言，遂以局殺湣公于蒙澤。

translations.literal: Wan was strong and resented these words, so he killed Duke Min with a game board at Mengze.
translations.idiomatic: Wan was a powerful man, and the insult stung. At Mengze, he struck Duke Min dead with a game board.

sentences.zh: 大夫仇牧聞之，以兵造公門。

translations.literal: Grand officer Qiu Mu heard of it and went to the gong's gate with troops.
translations.idiomatic: The grand officer Qiu Mu heard of it and went to the duke's gate with troops.

sentences.zh: 萬搏牧，牧齒著門闔死。

translations.literal: Wan wrestled with Mu. Mu's teeth bit the gate latch and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Wan struck Mu, whose teeth caught in the gate-leaves as he died.

sentences.zh: 因殺太宰華督，乃更立公子游為君。

translations.literal: He then killed Grand Steward Hua Du, and changed to establish Prince You as lord.
translations.idiomatic: He then killed the Grand Steward Hua Du, and changed to establish Prince You as lord.

sentences.zh: 諸公子奔蕭，公子御說奔亳。

translations.literal: The various princes fled to Xiao, and Prince Yuyue fled to Bo.
translations.idiomatic: The princes fled to Xiao, while Prince Yuyue fled to Bo.

sentences.zh: 萬弟南宮牛將兵圍亳。

translations.literal: Wan's younger brother Nangong Niu led troops and besieged Bo.
translations.idiomatic: Wan's younger brother Nangong Niu led an army to surround Bo.

sentences.zh: 冬，蕭及宋之諸公子共擊殺南宮牛，弒宋新君游而立湣公弟御說，是為桓公。

translations.literal: In winter, Xiao and Song's various princes together struck and killed Nangong Niu, assassinated Song's new lord You, and established Duke Min's younger brother Yu Yue, who became Duke Huan.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, Xiao and the princes of Song together attacked and killed Nangong Niu, assassinated Song's new lord You, and established Duke Min's younger brother Yushuo; this was Duke Huan.

sentences.zh: 宋萬奔陳。

translations.literal: Song Wan fled to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Song Wan fled to Chen.

sentences.zh: 宋人請以賂陳。

translations.literal: The Song people asked Chen to surrender him for a bribe.
translations.idiomatic: The Song people asked Chen to hand him over in exchange for a bribe.

sentences.zh: 陳人使婦人飲之醇酒，以革裹之，歸宋。

translations.literal: The Chen people made a woman drink him pure wine, wrapped him in leather, and returned him to Song.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen people made a woman give him pure wine to drink, wrapped him in leather, and returned him to Song.

sentences.zh: 宋人醢萬也。

translations.literal: The Song people minced Wan.
translations.idiomatic: The Song people minced Wan.

sentences.zh: 襄公七年，宋地茀星如雨，與雨偕下；

translations.literal: Xiang Gong seventh year, Song earth fell stars like rain, with rain together descended;
translations.idiomatic: In Duke Xiang's seventh year, stars fell over Song like rain, descending together with the rain.

sentences.zh: 六鶂退蜚，風疾也。

translations.literal: Six yi birds flew backward; the wind was fierce.
translations.idiomatic: Six yi birds were blown backward in flight, for the wind was violent.

sentences.zh: 八年，齊桓公卒，宋欲為盟會。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Duke Huan of Qi died, and Song wished to hold an alliance assembly.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, after Duke Huan of Qi died, Song sought to convene an alliance meeting.

sentences.zh: 十二年春，宋襄公為鹿上之盟，以求諸侯於楚，楚人許之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year spring, Duke Xiang of Song made the Lu Shang alliance to seek feudal lords from Chu. The Chu people permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, in spring, Duke Xiang of Song made the Lu Shang alliance to seek feudal lords from Chu. The Chu people permitted it.

sentences.zh: 公子目夷諫曰：「小國爭盟，禍也。」

translations.literal: Prince Mu Yi admonished said: 'Small state contends alliance, calamity.'
translations.idiomatic: Prince Muyi remonstrated and said: "For a small state to contend for leadership of the alliance is calamity."

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: He did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: He did not listen.

sentences.zh: 秋，諸侯會宋公盟于盂。

translations.literal: In autumn, the feudal lords met Duke Xiang of Song and made covenant at Yu.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the feudal lords met with Duke Xiang of Song and swore covenant at Yu.

sentences.zh: 目夷曰：「禍其在此乎？

translations.literal: Mu Yi said: 'Calamity perhaps here?
translations.idiomatic: Muyi said: "Is calamity perhaps here?

sentences.zh: 君欲已甚，何以堪之！」

translations.literal: Lord desire already excessive, what with endure it!'
translations.idiomatic: The lord's desire is excessive. How can this be endured!"

sentences.zh: 於是楚執宋襄公以伐宋。

translations.literal: Thereupon Chu seized Duke Xiang of Song and used him to attack Song.
translations.idiomatic: Chu then seized Duke Xiang of Song and used him as leverage in attacking Song.

sentences.zh: 冬，會于亳，以釋宋公。

translations.literal: In winter, they met at Bo in order to release the Duke of Song.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, they assembled at Bo and released the Duke of Song.

sentences.zh: 子魚曰：「禍猶未也。」

translations.literal: Zi Yu said: 'Calamity still not yet.'
translations.idiomatic: Ziyu said: "Calamity is still not yet."

sentences.zh: 十三年夏，宋伐鄭。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year summer, Song attacked Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, in summer, Song attacked Zheng.

sentences.zh: 子魚曰：「禍在此矣。」

translations.literal: Zi Yu said: 'Calamity here.'
translations.idiomatic: Ziyu said: "Calamity is here."

sentences.zh: 秋，楚伐宋以救鄭。

translations.literal: In autumn, Chu attacked Song in order to relieve Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, Chu attacked Song to relieve Zheng.

sentences.zh: 襄公將戰，子魚諫曰：「天之棄商久矣，不可。」

translations.literal: Xiang Gong about to battle, Zi Yu admonished said: 'Heaven abandoned Shang long ago, not permissible.'
translations.idiomatic: Duke Xiang was about to fight. Ziyu remonstrated and said: "Heaven abandoned Shang long ago. This must not be done."

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，襄公與楚成王戰于泓。

translations.literal: In winter, eleventh month, Duke Xiang battled with King Cheng of Chu at Hong.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the eleventh month, Duke Xiang battled with King Cheng of Chu at Hong.

sentences.zh: 楚人未濟，目夷曰：「彼眾我寡，及其未濟擊之。」

translations.literal: Chu people not yet crossed, Mu Yi said: 'They many we few, take advantage their not crossed strike them.'
translations.idiomatic: The Chu troops had not yet crossed. Muyi said: "They are many, we are few. Strike them while they have not yet crossed."

sentences.zh: 公不聽。

translations.literal: The gong did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The gong did not listen.

sentences.zh: 已濟未陳，又曰：「可擊。」

translations.literal: Already crossed not yet arrayed, again said: 'Can strike.'
translations.idiomatic: They had already crossed but were not yet arrayed. He again said: "We can strike."

sentences.zh: 公曰：「待其已陳。」

translations.literal: Gong said: 'Wait their already arrayed.'
translations.idiomatic: The duke said: "Wait until they are arrayed."

sentences.zh: 陳成，宋人擊之。

translations.literal: The array was completed. The Song people struck them.
translations.idiomatic: Only after the enemy array was complete did the Song men attack.

sentences.zh: 宋師大敗，襄公傷股。

translations.literal: The Song army was greatly defeated. Duke Xiang was wounded in the thigh.
translations.idiomatic: The Song army suffered a great defeat, and Duke Xiang was wounded in the thigh.

sentences.zh: 國人皆怨公。

translations.literal: The state people all resented the gong.
translations.idiomatic: The state people all resented the gong.

sentences.zh: 公曰：「君子不困人於阸，不鼓不成列。」

translations.literal: Gong said: 'Gentleman not distress people at narrow pass, not drum not formed ranks.'
translations.idiomatic: The duke said: "A gentleman does not press people in a narrow pass and does not beat the drums against ranks not yet formed."

sentences.zh: 子魚曰：「兵以勝為功，何常言與！

translations.literal: Zi Yu said: 'Warriors with victory as merit, what constant words with!
translations.idiomatic: Ziyu said: "In war, victory is the achievement. What fixed sayings are you invoking?

sentences.zh: 必如公言，即奴事之耳，又何戰為？」

translations.literal: Must be as the duke speaks, then slave and serve them—again what use is battle?'
translations.idiomatic: If we must follow your words, then we may as well submit and serve them as slaves. What is the use of battle?"

sentences.zh: 楚成王已救鄭，鄭享之；

translations.literal: Chu Cheng Wang already saved Zheng, Zheng feasted him;
translations.idiomatic: King Cheng of Chu had already saved Zheng, and Zheng feasted him;

sentences.zh: 去而取鄭二姬以歸。

translations.literal: He left and took two of Zheng's concubines and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He left and took two of Zheng's concubines and returned with them.

sentences.zh: 叔瞻曰：「成王無禮，其不沒乎？

translations.literal: Shu Zhan said: 'King Cheng is without ritual. Will he not perish?
translations.idiomatic: Shu Zhan said: "King Cheng has no sense of ritual. Will he not perish?

sentences.zh: 為禮卒於無別，有以知其不遂霸也。」

translations.literal: Making ritual end in lack of distinction, one has reason to know he will not succeed in hegemony.'
translations.idiomatic: When ritual ends with no distinctions, one can know that he will not succeed in becoming hegemon."

sentences.zh: 是年，晉公子重耳過宋，襄公以傷於楚，欲得晉援，厚禮重耳以馬二十乘。

translations.literal: This year, Jin's Prince Chong Er passed through Song. Duke Xiang, because wounded by Chu, desired to obtain Jin's aid. He thickly ritualed Chong Er with twenty chariots of horses.
translations.idiomatic: That year, Jin's Prince Chonger passed through Song. Duke Xiang, because he had been wounded by Chu, wished to obtain Jin's aid and treated Chonger generously with twenty teams of horses.

sentences.zh: 十四年夏，襄公病傷於泓而竟卒，子成公王臣立。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year summer, Duke Xiang's illness from being wounded at Hong finally caused him to die. His son Duke Cheng Wang Chen ascended.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, in summer, Duke Xiang finally died of the wound he had suffered at Hong. His son Duke Cheng Wangchen succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 十七年，成公卒。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, Duke Cheng died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, Duke Cheng died.

sentences.zh: 成公弟御殺太子及大司馬公孫固而自立為君。

translations.literal: Duke Cheng's younger brother Yu killed the crown prince and Grand Sima Gongsun Gu and self-established as lord.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Cheng's younger brother Yu killed the crown prince and Grand Marshal Gongsun Gu and established himself as lord.

sentences.zh: 宋人共殺君御而立成公少子杵臼，是為昭公。

translations.literal: The Song people together killed Lord Yu and established Duke Cheng's young son Chu Jiu, who became Duke Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Song together killed Lord Yu and established Duke Cheng's young son Chujiu; this was Duke Zhao.

sentences.zh: 九年，昭公無道，國人不附。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Duke Zhao lacked the Way, and the people of the state were not attached to him.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, Duke Zhao governed without principle, and the people of the state felt no loyalty to him.

sentences.zh: 昭公弟鮑革賢而下士。

translations.literal: Duke Zhao's younger brother Bao Ge was worthy and humble toward gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Zhao's younger brother Bao Ge was capable and treated worthy men with humility.

sentences.zh: 先，襄公夫人欲通於公子鮑，不可，乃助之施於國，因大夫華元為右師。

translations.literal: Previously, Duke Xiang's wife wished to have an affair with Prince Bao. He would not agree, so she helped him bestow favors throughout the state and secured Grand Officer Hua Yuan as Right Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, Duke Xiang's wife wished to have an affair with Prince Bao. He would not agree, so she helped him distribute favors throughout the state and secured Grand Officer Hua Yuan as Right Minister.

sentences.zh: 昭公出獵，夫人王姬使衛伯攻殺昭公杵臼。

translations.literal: Duke Zhao went hunting. His wife Wang Ji made Wei Bo attack and kill Duke Zhao Chu Jiu.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Zhao went hunting. His wife Wang Ji made Wei Bo attack and kill the Duke Zhao Chu Jiu.

sentences.zh: 弟鮑革立，是為文公。

translations.literal: His younger brother Bao Ge was established; this was Duke Wen.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Bao Ge was installed as Duke Wen.

sentences.zh: 四年春，（鄭）［楚］命（楚）［鄭］伐宋。

translations.literal: In the fourth year spring, Zheng commanded Chu to attack Song.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, in spring, Chu commanded Zheng to attack Song.

sentences.zh: 宋使華元將，鄭敗宋，囚華元。

translations.literal: Song had Hua Yuan command the army; Zheng defeated Song and captured Hua Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Song placed Hua Yuan in command, but Zheng defeated Song and took Hua Yuan prisoner.

sentences.zh: 華元之將戰，殺羊以食士，其御羊羹不及，故怨，馳入鄭軍，故宋師敗，得囚華元。

translations.literal: Hua Yuan was about to battle. He killed a sheep to feed the soldiers. His driver did not obtain mutton soup, so he resented it. He galloped into the Zheng army. Therefore, the Song army was defeated, and they obtained and imprisoned Hua Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Hua Yuan was about to fight, he slaughtered a sheep to feed the soldiers. His driver did not receive any mutton soup and resented it, so he drove straight into the Zheng army. The Song army was therefore defeated, and Zheng captured Hua Yuan.

sentences.zh: 宋以兵車百乘文馬四百匹贖華元。

translations.literal: Song redeemed Hua Yuan with one hundred war chariots and four hundred patterned horses.
translations.idiomatic: Song ransomed Hua Yuan with a hundred war chariots and four hundred fine horses.

sentences.zh: 未盡入，華元亡歸宋。

translations.literal: They had not completely entered. Hua Yuan fled and returned to Song.
translations.idiomatic: They had not all entered. Hua Yuan fled and returned to Song.

sentences.zh: 十四年，楚莊王圍鄭。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, King Zhuang of Chu besieged Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, King Zhuang of Chu laid siege to Zheng.

sentences.zh: 鄭伯降楚，楚復釋之。

translations.literal: The Earl of Zheng surrendered to Chu, and Chu then released him.
translations.idiomatic: The Earl of Zheng surrendered to Chu, and Chu released him again.

sentences.zh: 十六年，楚使過宋，宋有前仇，執楚使。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, a Chu envoy passed through Song; Song had an earlier grievance and seized the Chu envoy.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, a Chu envoy passed through Song. Because of an old grievance, Song detained him.

sentences.zh: 九月，楚莊王圍宋。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, King Zhuang of Chu besieged Song.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, King Zhuang of Chu laid siege to Song.

sentences.zh: 十七年，楚以圍宋五月不解，宋城中急，無食，華元乃夜私見楚將子反。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, Chu, because they had besieged Song for five months without releasing it, the Song city was urgent with no food. Hua Yuan then at night privately saw the Chu general Zi Fan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, Chu had besieged Song for five months without releasing it. The Song city was urgent with no food. Hua Yuan then at night privately saw the Chu general Zi Fan.

sentences.zh: 子反告莊王。

translations.literal: Zi Fan told King Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Zi Fan told King Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 王問：「城中何如？」

translations.literal: Wang asked: 'City middle what like?'
translations.idiomatic: The king asked: "What is it like inside the city?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「析骨而炊，易子而食。」

translations.literal: Said: 'Split bones and cook, exchange children and eat.'
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "They split bones for fuel and exchange children to eat."

sentences.zh: 莊王曰：「誠哉言！

translations.literal: Zhuang Wang said: 'Truly words!
translations.idiomatic: King Zhuang said: "True words!

sentences.zh: 我軍亦有二日糧。」

translations.literal: Our army also has two days grain.'
translations.idiomatic: Our army also has only two days of grain."

sentences.zh: 以信故，遂罷兵去。

translations.literal: Because of trust, they then withdrew the army and left.
translations.idiomatic: Because of mutual trust, they then withdrew the army and left.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，文公卒，子共公瑕立。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, Duke Wen died, and his son Xia, Duke Gong, succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year, Duke Wen died and was succeeded by his son Xia, Duke Gong.

sentences.zh: 始厚葬。

translations.literal: They began thick burials.
translations.idiomatic: They began thick burials.

sentences.zh: 君子譏華元不臣矣。

translations.literal: The gentleman criticized Hua Yuan for not being a minister.
translations.idiomatic: The gentleman criticized Hua Yuan for failing in a minister's duty.

sentences.zh: 共公（元）［十］年，華元善楚將子重，又善晉將欒書，兩盟晉楚。

translations.literal: In Duke Gong's tenth year, Hua Yuan was good with Chu's general Zi Zhong, and also good with Jin's general Luan Shu. He allied both Jin and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: In Duke Gong's tenth year, Hua Yuan was friendly with Chu's general Zizhong and also with Jin's general Luan Shu. He made alliances with both Jin and Chu.

sentences.zh: 十三年，共公卒。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Duke Gong died.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, Duke Gong died.

sentences.zh: 華元為右師，魚石為左師。

translations.literal: Hua Yuan served as Right Master, and Yu Shi served as Left Master.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Yuan became Right Master, and Yu Shi became Left Master.

sentences.zh: 司馬唐山攻殺太子肥，欲殺華元，華元奔晉，魚石止之，至河乃還，誅唐山。

translations.literal: Sima Tang Shan attacked and killed Crown Prince Fei. He desired to kill Hua Yuan. Hua Yuan fled to Jin. Yu Shi stopped him. He reached the river and then returned. They executed Tang Shan.
translations.idiomatic: Marshal Tangshan attacked and killed Crown Prince Fei and wanted to kill Hua Yuan. Hua Yuan fled to Jin, but Yu Shi stopped him; when he reached the river, he returned. They executed Tangshan.

sentences.zh: 乃立共公少子成，是為平公。

translations.literal: They then established Duke Gong's younger son Cheng; this was Duke Ping.
translations.idiomatic: They then installed Cheng, the younger son of Duke Gong, as Duke Ping.

sentences.zh: 平公三年，楚共王拔宋之彭城，以封宋左師魚石。

translations.literal: In Duke Ping's third year, Chu's King Gong seized Song's Peng Cheng to enfeoff Song's left teacher Yu Shi.
translations.idiomatic: In Duke Ping's third year, King Gong of Chu seized Song's Pengcheng and enfeoffed Song's Left Minister Yu Shi there.

sentences.zh: 四年，諸侯共誅魚石，而歸彭城於宋。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the feudal lords jointly punished Yu Shi and returned Pengcheng to Song.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, the feudal lords together put down Yu Shi and restored Pengcheng to Song.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，楚公子圍弒其君自立，為靈王。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year, Chu's Prince Wei assassinated his lord and self-established as King Ling.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year, Chu's Prince Wei assassinated his lord and established himself as King Ling.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，平公卒，子元公佐立。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year, Duke Ping died, and his son Duke Yuan Zuo ascended.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fourth year, Duke Ping died, and his son Duke Yuan Zuo succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 元公三年，楚公子棄疾弒靈王，自立為平王。

translations.literal: In Duke Yuan's third year, Chu's Prince Qi Ji assassinated King Ling and self-established as King Ping.
translations.idiomatic: In Duke Yuan's third year, Chu's Prince Qiji assassinated King Ling and established himself as King Ping.

sentences.zh: 八年，宋火。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Song suffered a fire.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, a fire broke out in Song.

sentences.zh: 十年，元公毋信，詐殺諸公子，大夫華、向氏作亂。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Duke Yuan had no trust. He falsely killed the various princes. The grand officers of the Hua and Xiang clans made rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, Duke Yuan was untrustworthy and falsely killed the princes. The grand officers of the Hua and Xiang clans rebelled.

sentences.zh: 楚平王太子建來奔，見諸華氏相攻亂，建去如鄭。

translations.literal: Chu's King Ping's crown prince Jian came fleeing. He saw the various Hua clans mutually attacking in chaos. Jian left and went to Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: King Ping of Chu's crown prince Jian fled to Song. Seeing the Hua clans attacking each other in chaos, Jian left and went to Zheng.

sentences.zh: 十五年，元公為魯昭公避季氏居外，為之求入魯，行道卒，子景公頭曼立。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, Duke Yuan, for Lu's Duke Zhao, avoided the Ji clan and resided outside. He sought for him to enter Lu. Traveling on the road, he died. His son Duke Jing Tou Man ascended.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, Duke Yuan was living outside Lu on behalf of Duke Zhao of Lu, who had fled the Ji clan, and sought to restore him to Lu. He died while traveling, and his son Duke Jing Touman succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 景公十六年，魯陽虎來奔，已復去。

translations.literal: In Duke Jing's sixteenth year, Lu's Yang Hu came fleeing, then again left.
translations.idiomatic: In Duke Jing's sixteenth year, Lu's Yang Hu fled here, then again left the state.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，孔子過宋，宋司馬桓魋惡之，欲殺孔子，孔子微服去。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, Kong Qiu passed through Song. Song's Sima Huan Dai hated him and desired to kill Kong Qiu. Kong Qiu disguised himself and left.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year, Confucius passed through Song. Song's Marshal Huan Tui hated him and wanted to kill him. Confucius disguised himself and left.

sentences.zh: 三十年，曹倍宋，又倍晉，宋伐曹，晉不救，遂滅曹有之。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, Cao betrayed Song and then betrayed Jin; Song attacked Cao, Jin did not rescue it, and Song then destroyed Cao and possessed it.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year, Cao betrayed Song and then Jin. Song attacked Cao; Jin did not come to its rescue, and Song destroyed Cao and annexed it.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，齊田常弒簡公。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year, Tian Chang of Qi killed Duke Jian.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-sixth year, Tian Chang of Qi assassinated Duke Jian.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，楚惠王滅陳。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year, King Hui of Chu destroyed Chen.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-seventh year, King Hui of Chu conquered Chen.

sentences.zh: 熒惑守心。

translations.literal: Ying Huo guarded Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Huo guarded Xin.

sentences.zh: 心，宋之分野也。

translations.literal: Xin is Song's celestial region.
translations.idiomatic: Xin was Song's corresponding celestial field.

sentences.zh: 景公憂之。

translations.literal: Duke Jing worried about it.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Jing worried about it.

sentences.zh: 司星子韋曰：「可移於相。」

translations.literal: Si Xing Zi Wei said: 'Can move to prime minister.'
translations.idiomatic: The astrologer Ziwei said: "It can be shifted to the chancellor."

sentences.zh: 景公曰：「相，吾之股肱。」

translations.literal: Jing Gong said: 'Prime minister, my limbs.'
translations.idiomatic: Duke Jing said: "The chancellor is my arms and legs."

sentences.zh: 曰：「可移於民。」

translations.literal: Said: 'Can move to people.'
translations.idiomatic: He said: "It can be shifted to the people."

sentences.zh: 景公曰：「君者待民。」

translations.literal: Jing Gong said: 'Lord relies on people.'
translations.idiomatic: Duke Jing said: "A lord depends on the people."

sentences.zh: 曰：「可移於歲。」

translations.literal: Said: 'Can move to year.'
translations.idiomatic: He said: "It can be shifted to the year."

sentences.zh: 景公曰：「歲饑民困，吾誰為君！」

translations.literal: Jing Gong said: 'Year famine people distressed, I for whom be lord!'
translations.idiomatic: Duke Jing said: "If the year is famine-stricken and the people are distressed, for whom would I be lord!"

sentences.zh: 子韋曰：「天高聽卑。

translations.literal: Zi Wei said: 'Heaven high hears low.
translations.idiomatic: Zi Wei said: "Heaven is high but hears the low.

sentences.zh: 君有君人之言三，熒惑宜有動。」

translations.literal: Lord has lord people words three, Ying Huo should have movement.'
translations.idiomatic: The lord has spoken three sayings worthy of one who rules the people. Mars should move."

sentences.zh: 於是候之，果徙三度。

translations.literal: Thereupon they watched for it, and indeed it shifted three degrees.
translations.idiomatic: They then observed it, and it did indeed move three degrees.

sentences.zh: 六十四年，景公卒。

translations.literal: In the sixty-fourth year, Duke Jing died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixty-fourth year, Duke Jing died.

sentences.zh: 宋公子特攻殺太子而自立，是為昭公。

translations.literal: Song's Prince Te attacked and killed the crown prince and self-established, who became Duke Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Song's Prince Te attacked and killed the crown prince and established himself; this was Duke Zhao.

sentences.zh: 昭公者，元公之曾庶孫也。

translations.literal: Duke Zhao was a great-grandson of Duke Yuan through a lesser line.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Zhao was Duke Yuan's great-grandson through a collateral line.

sentences.zh: 昭公父公孫糾，糾父公子褍秦，褍秦即元公少子也。

translations.literal: Duke Zhao's father was Gongsun Jiu. Jiu's father was Prince Ju Qin. Ju Qin was Duke Yuan's young son.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Zhao's father was Gongsun Jiu. Jiu's father was Prince Duanqin. Duanqin was Duke Yuan's younger son.

sentences.zh: 景公殺昭公父糾，故昭公怨殺太子而自立。

translations.literal: Duke Jing killed Duke Zhao's father Jiu. Therefore, Duke Zhao resented it, killed the crown prince, and self-established.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Jing had killed Duke Zhao's father Jiu. Duke Zhao therefore resented it, killed the crown prince, and established himself.

sentences.zh: 昭公四十七年卒，子悼公購由立。

translations.literal: Duke Zhao died in his forty-seventh year, and his son Duke Dao Gou You ascended.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Zhao died in his forty-seventh year, and his son Duke Dao Gou You succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 悼公八年卒，子休公田立。

translations.literal: Duke Dao died in his eighth year, and his son Duke Xiu Tian ascended.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Dao died in his eighth year, and his son Duke Xiu Tian succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 休公田二十三年卒，子辟公辟兵立。

translations.literal: Duke Xiu Tian died in his twenty-third year, and his son Duke Bi Bi Bing ascended.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Xiu Tian died in his twenty-third year, and his son the Duke Bi Bi Bing succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 辟公三年卒，子剔成立。

translations.literal: Duke Bi died in his third year, and his son Ti Cheng ascended.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Bi died in his third year, and his son Ti Cheng succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 剔成四十一年，剔成弟偃攻襲剔成，剔成敗奔齊，偃自立為宋君。

translations.literal: In Ti Cheng's forty-first year, Ti Cheng's younger brother Yan attacked and raided Ti Cheng. Ti Cheng was defeated and fled to Qi. Yan self-established as Song's lord.
translations.idiomatic: In Ti Cheng's forty-first year, Ti Cheng's younger brother Yan attacked Ti Cheng by surprise. Ti Cheng was defeated and fled to Qi. Yan established himself as lord of Song.

sentences.zh: 君偃十一年，自立為王。

translations.literal: In Lord Yan's eleventh year, he self-established as wang.
translations.idiomatic: In Lord Yan's eleventh year, he declared himself king.

sentences.zh: 東敗齊，取五城；

translations.literal: East defeated Qi, took five cities;
translations.idiomatic: In the east he defeated Qi and took five cities;

sentences.zh: 南敗楚，取地三百里；

translations.literal: South defeated Chu, took land three hundred li;
translations.idiomatic: In the south he defeated Chu and took land three hundred li;

sentences.zh: 西敗魏軍，乃與齊、魏為敵國。

translations.literal: In the west he defeated Wei's army, and then became an enemy state with Qi and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the west he defeated Wei's army and then became an enemy of Qi and Wei.

sentences.zh: 盛血以韋囊，縣而射之，命曰「射天」。

translations.literal: Filled blood with leather bag, hung and shot it, named 'shoot heaven'.
translations.idiomatic: He filled a leather bag with blood, hung it up, and shot it, calling this "shooting Heaven."

sentences.zh: 淫於酒婦人。

translations.literal: He was licentious with wine and women.
translations.idiomatic: He was licentious with wine and women.

sentences.zh: 群臣諫者輒射之。

translations.literal: Whenever ministers remonstrated, he shot them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever ministers tried to remonstrate, he shot them.

sentences.zh: 於是諸侯皆曰「桀宋」。

translations.literal: Then the feudal lords all said, 'Song is [like] Jie.'
translations.idiomatic: Then the feudal lords all said, "Song is like Jie."

sentences.zh: 「宋其復為紂所為，不可不誅」。

translations.literal: 'Song will again do what Zhou did; it cannot go unpunished.'
translations.idiomatic: "Song is again doing what Zhou did; it cannot go unpunished."

sentences.zh: 告齊伐宋。

translations.literal: They informed Qi to attack Song.
translations.idiomatic: They informed Qi to attack Song.

sentences.zh: 王偃立四十七年，齊湣王與魏、楚伐宋，殺王偃，遂滅宋而三分其地。

translations.literal: Wang Yan ascended for forty-seven years. Qi's King Min with Wei and Chu attacked Song, killed Wang Yan, then extinguished Song and divided its land into three.
translations.idiomatic: In Wang Yan's forty-seventh year, King Min of Qi, together with Wei and Chu, attacked Song, killed Wang Yan, extinguished Song, and divided its territory into three parts.

sentences.zh: 太史公曰：孔子稱「微子去之，箕子為之奴，比干諫而死，殷有三仁焉」。

translations.literal: Grand Historian said: Kong Qiu praised 'Wei Zi left it, jizi became slave for it, Bi Gan admonished and died, Yin had three benevolent.'
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Historian said: Confucius praised them: "Weizi left, Jizi became a slave, and Bi Gan remonstrated and died. Yin had three benevolent men."

sentences.zh: 春秋譏宋之亂自宣公廢太子而立弟，國以不寧者十世。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals criticized Song's chaos from Duke Xuan deposing the crown prince and establishing his younger brother. The state was not peaceful for ten generations.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals criticized Song's chaos as beginning when Duke Xuan deposed the crown prince and established his younger brother. For ten generations the state had no peace.

sentences.zh: 襄公之時，修行仁義，欲為盟主。

translations.literal: In Duke Xiang's time, he cultivated benevolence and righteousness and wished to become leader of the alliance.
translations.idiomatic: In Duke Xiang's time, he cultivated benevolence and righteousness and aspired to lead the interstate alliance.

sentences.zh: 其大夫正考父美之，故追道契、湯、高宗，殷所以興，作商頌。

translations.literal: His grand officer Zheng Kao Fu praised this, therefore traced the way of Qi, Tang, and Gaozong—how Yin rose—and composed the Shang Song.
translations.idiomatic: His grand officer Zheng Kao Fu praised this; therefore he traced the way of Qi, Tang, and Gaozong—how Yin rose—and composed the Shang Song.

sentences.zh: 襄公既敗於泓，而君子或以為多，傷中國闕禮義，褒之也，宋襄之有禮讓也。」」」」」」」」」」」

translations.literal: Duke Xiang had already been defeated at Hong, yet some gentlemen considered his courtesy excessive, grieving that China lacked ritual and righteousness; they praised him—Duke Xiang of Song had ritual and yielding.”
translations.idiomatic: Duke Xiang had already been defeated at Hong, yet some gentlemen considered his courtesy excessive, grieving that the central states lacked ritual and righteousness; they praised him—Duke Xiang of Song had ritual and yielding.”
